name: Toyota MR2 (SW20)
engine: 2.0L turbocharged I4 (3S-GTE) on the Turbo · 2.2L NA I4 (5S-FE) on the base US car
torque: 200 lb-ft @ 3,200 rpm (US Turbo); JDM Rev3/Rev4 cars made ~245 PS / 224 lb-ft
transmission: 5-speed manual (a 4-speed automatic was offered on lower trims)
reliability: 8/10 — the 3S-GTE is a stout, iron-block turbo four that responds hugely to boost and takes abuse well, and the SW20 is generally dependable for a 30-year-old mid-engine sports car. The famous asterisk is handling, not the engine: the early Rev1 cars (1991–1992) had genuine snap-oversteer that Toyota fixed with wider rear tires and revised suspension from Rev2 on. The other realities are age-related — cooling lines that run the length of the car, and turbo/clutch wear on hard-used examples. A sorted later-revision car is a joy.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate–High (turbo sports coupe, rising values) · Maintenance ~$600/yr and climbing as parts get scarce · Clean Turbos are appreciating collector cars now, so originality and history pay
popular_mods: A Rev2+ suspension setup or quality coilovers with a proper alignment — tames the early cars' tail
A larger front-mount intercooler and boost controller — the 3S-GTE loves air and responds fast
A CT20b or aftermarket turbo upgrade for owners chasing 300+ hp reliably
Fresh coolant hard-lines and hoses — the long mid-engine cooling runs are a known age item
Honest take: fix the chassis and cooling first; the engine will happily make power once the basics are sorted
oil_interval: Every 3,000–5,000 miles (shorter on a boosted, tracked car)

generations.Rev1 (1991–1992 US): The original SW20 Turbo — 200 hp, sharp looks, and the notorious lift-off snap-oversteer from narrow rear tires and the mid-engine mass. Thrilling but demands respect.
generations.Rev2 (1993–1995 US): The fix: wider rear tires, revised suspension geometry, bigger brakes, and a stiffer body. Much more planted and the sweet spot for US buyers.
generations.Rev3–Rev5 (1994–1999 JDM): Japan kept the car alive with more power (~245 PS), a stronger gearbox, and detail improvements. These later JDM Turbos are the most desirable SW20s and increasingly imported.

common_issues: Rev1 snap (lift-off) oversteer — a chassis trait, resolved from Rev2 onward
Aging mid-engine cooling system — the long coolant hard-lines and hoses corrode and leak with age
Turbo and clutch wear on hard-driven or boosted cars; verify boost history
Rust on early cars in salt climates — check the rockers, floors, and rear frame
Parts scarcity for some Turbo-specific and interior pieces as the cars age
maintenance_tips: Refresh the entire cooling system (hard-lines, hoses, thermostat) on any car with unknown history
Keep boost sensible on a stock engine and use good synthetic oil — the 3S-GTE is tough but heat-sensitive
Fit later-spec suspension or a proper alignment before pushing an early car hard
Inspect the clutch and check for even, healthy boost with no smoke on spool-up
Preserve originality and paperwork — later JDM revisions and clean US Turbos are appreciating fast

engine.detail: Iron-block 2.0L 3S-GTE turbo four (200 hp / 200 lb-ft) on the Turbo; base US cars got the 2.2L NA 5S-FE.
engine.watch: The signature age item is the long mid-engine coolant hard-lines corroding and leaking; it also weeps oil from the cam cover and distributor o-rings.

drivetrain.detail: Mid-engine, transverse, RWD through a 5-speed manual (E153); later cars added a limited-slip diff.
drivetrain.watch: Clutch and turbo wear on hard-driven or over-boosted cars - verify boost history and a clean, smoke-free spool-up.

suspension.detail: Struts at all four corners behind the driver; Rev2 (1993+) added wider rear tires and revised geometry.
suspension.watch: Early Rev1 (1991-92) cars are the infamous snap/lift-off oversteer cars; fit later-spec suspension or at least a proper alignment.

brakes.detail: Four-wheel discs, upsized on the Turbo and again from Rev2.
brakes.watch: No design flaw, just age - check for warped rotors and tired flex lines on a 30-year-old car.

electrical.detail: Conventional early-90s Toyota electrics, with the alternator tucked low in a tight mid-engine bay.
electrical.watch: Oil leaks from above drip onto the alternator and cook it - and it's a miserable job to swap in that cramped bay.

body.detail: Steel unibody coupe with an optional T-bar removable roof.
body.watch: Early cars rust in salt climates - inspect the rockers, floors, and rear frame rails before buying.
